MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 P-H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.44.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the First and Last Frame version of MiniMax H3 (fl2va): if you did Episode 41 you may already have it.

 LoRA (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

Download p-h3-image_lora_bf16.safetensors1.82 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download p-h3-image_text_encoder_int8_convrot.safetensors4.77 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download p-h3-image_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.93 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 License

P-H3 Image is built on MiniMax H3, so the MiniMax H3 Community License applies. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model.

READ LICENSE P-H3 Image model page 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.183). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Give the model a small picture and it draws it again, bigger and sharper. This is a creative upscale: it does not stretch your pixels, it paints a new picture that follows yours, so small details can come out different. There is no upscale model to download: P-H3 Image does the job itself. The demo takes a small 3D picture of 410 x 512 pixels and makes it 1824 x 2304.

 Steps

  1. Load your small picture in Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. Leave the prompt as it is.
  3. Click a size on Number Pick Pixaroma.
  4. Leave the seed on F to repeat a result, or switch it to R to try a new one every Run.
  5. Press Run. Drag across Image Compare Pixaroma to see before and after.

 Why your picture goes in small

Your picture goes to PH3 Image Conditioning as it is. Scale Image to Total Pixels and Get Image Size only work out the new size. A picture that was enlarged first is blurry, and the model copies that blur. Given the small one, it has to draw the fine detail itself, so the result comes out sharper, and faster too.

 Writing the prompt

  1. The demo prompt works on any picture, because it names nothing that is in it. Start with that one.
  2. Only name what is really there. Our first prompt asked for fine skin and the same faces. On a picture of a shop with no people in it, the model painted a face over the shop on 3 of 4 seeds.

 Good to know

  • 3D pictures and fur work best. In the demo the fur and the cookies came out sharp on 4 of 4 seeds. The eyes came out a little bigger than in the small picture, and on 3 of 4 seeds a small pink tongue appeared above the cookie.
  • The size of your picture decides how much is new. We shrank a portrait of a woman to test this. From 1024 pixels she stayed the same woman, with her freckles. From 512 pixels the hands stayed right on 4 of 4 seeds, but most of the freckles went and the eyebrows and lashes came out darker. From 256 pixels it drew a different looking woman on 2 of 2 seeds.
  • Big words stay right, small ones do not. On a bakery, the big shop name was right on 4 of 4 seeds. The small handwritten line under it had wrong letters on 3 of 4, and its year was hard to read on all 4.
  • Old photos keep their damage. On a scratched sepia family photo, 4 of 4 seeds kept the sepia colour and the scratches, and drew them sharper. To repair an old photo, use workflow 8.
  • Start with 4 megapixels. The detail grows a lot from 1 to 4. On the demo, 8 megapixels took about twice as long and was sharper on only 1 of 3 seeds.
  • The colours and the framing stay. On 18 test runs the colours moved very little, and the picture stayed within 16 pixels of where it was.
  • The result has the shape of your picture. The demo goes in at 410 x 512 and comes out at 1824 x 2304.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 fl2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. The LoRA in the next node turns it into P-H3 Image, a picture model. If you did Episode 41 you may already have this file.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (P-H3 Image) - The P-H3 Image LoRA from Pruna. Keep it on at strength 1: without it H3 is a video model and the picture falls apart.
  • Load CLIP (P-H3 Image text encoder) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the model understands. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (P-H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for P-H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your small picture) - The small picture to make bigger. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (2. leave it for most pictures) - This prompt names nothing in the picture, so it works on any picture. You can leave it as it is (see How to Use).
  • Number Pick Pixaroma (3. megapixels) - How big the result is. Click 1, 2, 4 (the demo) or 8 megapixels. A square picture comes out at 1024, 1440, 2048 or 2912 pixels on each side. A smaller size is faster.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) repeats the result, R (random) tries a new one every Run. The demo uses seed 4.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (1 / 1 for pictures) - The noise schedule. P-H3 Image needs 1 and 1. Leave it as it is.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels (works out the new size) - Works out the size of the result from the number you clicked on Number Pick Pixaroma. Only the size is used: your picture goes to the conditioning small, on purpose (see How to Use).
  • Get Image Size (the size of the result) - Reads the width and height of the scaled picture and hands them to the conditioning.
  • PH3 Image Conditioning (prompt + your picture) - Joins the prompt and your small picture. width and height come from Get Image Size, so the new picture is drawn at the big size.
  • Basic Guider (no CFG) - Hands the model and the prompt to the sampler. P-H3 Image needs no CFG and no negative prompt.
  • KSampler Select (sampler) - The sampler. euler is the one in Pruna's own workflow. ComfyUI's template uses er_sde: the same speed, but it broke small words on a label in our tests.
  • Manual Sigmas (the 8 steps) - The 8 steps the model was trained on. More steps do not help, so leave these numbers as they are.
  • Random Noise - The starting noise, from the seed.
  • Sampler Custom Advanced (the render) - The render itself: 8 steps. The normal KSampler cannot take this hand-made step list, so this node does the job.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the result) - Saves each result as PNG into ComfyUI/output/P-H3 Image Creative Upscale and shows it on the node.
  • Image Compare Pixaroma (before and after, drag across it) - Your small picture and the result on top of each other. Drag across it to see the new detail.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is much faster.

SizeTime
1 megapixel3 to 6 s
2 megapixels5 to 8 s
4 megapixels (the demo)11 to 21 s
8 megapixels32 to 38 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3, and 10 GB for the LoRA, the text encoder and the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it. Two testers with 16 GB cards: with 64 GB of RAM the next Runs were close to the times above; with 32 GB the models loaded from disk again on every Run, and each Run took about 4 times as long.

 On a smaller card

Click 1 or 2 on Number Pick Pixaroma.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
